summary: Feature request to add a configurable workflow-status filter to Temporal's archival system, allowing operators to archive only specific workflow statuses (e.g., failed, timed out) instead of all closed workflows, reducing storage costs at scale.
userImpact: OSS users self-hosting on AWS S3 can dramatically reduce monthly archival costs (from ~$37,500 to near-zero) by filtering which workflow statuses are archived.
rootCause: Temporal archives all closed workflows by default regardless of status, but most deployments only need failures for debugging; with 50M workflows/day and 5 storage PUTs per workflow, this results in 7.5B unnecessary PUTs/month.
proposedFix: Add optional `statusFilter` configuration at archiver provider level that short-circuits Archive() calls for workflows not in the allowlist, with independent filters for history and visibility archival.
workaround: Users can fork temporal-server and implement filtering in custom archiver wrapper code, or run a sidecar service that copies only failed workflows to S3.
keyQuote: ~90% of those requests are for successful workflows that exit retention without ever being inspected.
